title: Network card, repeater, bridge and gateway

videos.script: Lesson 1 named the big boxes. This one is about four words that sit underneath them. {{words}} The network card is where a cable meets a computer. It has an address of six bytes, and two bits in the first byte change what that address means. {{card}} You will read a card's counters before and after five pings, and see why the numbers never match the pings exactly. {{counters}} The repeater only makes a cable longer. The bridge is older than the switch, and it is what a switch still is underneath. In the lab you will watch one learn three addresses from two pings. {{bridge}} Then the gateway. In a configuration it is not a box, it is an address. You will capture a frame leaving a computer for a server two networks away, and see that the frame is addressed to the router, not to the server. {{frame}} Last, a mistake made on purpose. One computer gets a gateway that nobody has. Its own network keeps working, everything else fails, and the error message comes from its own address. {{wrong}} By the end you will read that message and know which line of the configuration to check.
